raw_response:
I'm Old Wang, 59 this year, been farming since I was 14. Never went to school, can't read, but I know my land. I've got 10.7 mu, same plot my father farmed. Wheat in the fall, maize right after the wheat comes off — that's how it's always been. My wife helps, my two grown children work in the factory in Handan, send a bit back sometimes, but they're not here for the busy season. So it's mostly me and the old woman.

**What I'm thinking about this year:**

The wheat — I plant around October 8th, give or take, when the soil feels right. I use the same improved wheat seed I've been using, about 25 jin per mu. I don't save my own wheat seed anymore, buy from the supply shop in town, costs about 50 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that's what I've done for years, what my neighbor does too. Then at jointing, when the wheat starts moving, I topdress with urea, about 40 jin per mu total split in my head however I carry it. The soil's decent but not rich. I irrigate three times: once before winter so it doesn't dry out, once at jointing in March, and once when the grain is filling in May. The pump costs money, electricity isn't cheap, but you can't skip it. For weeds, I spray herbicide once after planting, that's about 15 yuan per mu. I don't usually need insecticide for wheat.

The maize — this is the hard part. Wheat comes off around June 10th, and I got maybe five days to get the maize in the ground. I hire a tractor for rotary till, costs me, but I can't do it by hand that fast. I buy hybrid maize seed, can't save it, costs about 45 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer down at planting, again about half a bag per mu. If it rains good in July, maybe I only irrigate once at the big trumpet stage. If it's dry like two years ago, twice. I spray herbicide once when the maize is small, and watch for worms — if I see them, I spray, but I try not to spend too much. I hope for 450 jin per mu, last year I got about 420.

Money's tight. My total cash for inputs this season is maybe 6,000 yuan. I have to be careful. I use family labor for most things, but for wheat harvest and maize planting in that tight window, I might need to hire one person for a couple days. Every yuan I spend on fertilizer is a yuan I don't have for medicine or emergencies. But I'm also scared of not putting enough — a bad yield means borrowing money. So I stick to what I know: about the same as last year, maybe a tiny bit less fertilizer if prices went up.
